For Petitioners : Mr.T.V.Vineeth Kumar
For Respondents : Mrs.Rita Chandrasekar
COMMON ORDER

The relief sought for in the present writ petition is to direct the 1st respondent to consider the representations of the petitioners dated 04.07.2023, 05.07.2023 and 12.07.2023 and fix the compensation only the the owners of 4731 sq.ft bearing Door No.55, Arcot Road, New No.97, N.S.K.
Salai, Kodambakkam, Chennai  600024.
2.
It is not in dispute that the land belonged to the petitioners was acquired for the purpose of Chennai Metro Rail Project.

The Acquisition https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.26550 &
26552 of 2023 proceedings commenced and the award is yet to be passed by the competent authority.
The grievances of the writ petitioners is that the adjacent lands are also taken and compensation has been paid to those owners and the petitioners are deprived of fair compensation.

3. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Chennai Metro Rail Limited raised an objection by stating that the land belonged to the petitioners was acquired and the authorities are in the process of determining the compensation, since private negotiation has failed.

On determination of compensation, an award will be passed and the petitioners are at liberty to participate in the award proceedings and raise objections, if any, for the purpose of considering the same by the competent authorities.
4. In view of the said submission, the petitioners are at liberty to participate in the award proceedings and file their objections regarding quantum of compensation to be settled.
The authorities shall consider the objections in accordance with the procedure contemplated under the Land Acquisition Act and pass an award without causing any undue delay.

Thereafter, if the petitioners are aggrieved, they are at liberty to seek https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.26550 & 26552 of 2023 enhancement of compensation in the manner contemplated under the Act.
However, the present writ petitions, at this stage, are premature and thus not entertainable.
5. Accordingly, the Writ Petitions stand dismissed.
No costs.
